body_markdown:
A domiciliary account used to feel like the only way to receive US dollars in Nigeria. If someone wanted to pay you in USD, the usual advice was, “Open a domiciliary account first.” Today, that’s no longer your only option.


Whether you’re a freelancer, remote employee, creator, founder, or online entrepreneur, receiving USD has become much easier. Instead of navigating paperwork, bank visits, and the limitations that often come with a domiciliary account, you can now access modern payment solutions built for the way people earn today.


In this guide, you’ll learn when a domiciliary account makes sense, why many Nigerians are looking for alternatives, and how[Cleva](http://www.getcleva.com/) helps you receive and manage USD payments with real US banking details, all without opening a traditional domiciliary account.


## **What is a domiciliary account?**


A domiciliary account is a bank account that allows you to receive, hold, and send foreign currencies such as US dollars, British pounds, or euros.


For years, Nigerians relied on these type of accounts to receive international payments from employers, clients, relatives, and business partners abroad.


Unlike a regular naira account, domiciliary accounts lets you keep funds in foreign currency instead of converting them immediately.


While that can be useful, it isn’t always the most convenient option for people who receive USD frequently.


## **Why many Nigerians want an alternative to a domiciliary account**


Although traditional banking options can serve certain needs, many people find the experience less flexible than they expected.


Some common challenges include:


- Lengthy account opening requirements
- Multiple verification documents
- Branch visits during setup
- Longer processing times
- Limited integration with modern global payment platforms


For freelancers and remote workers who need fast, reliable access to USD earnings, these hurdles can slow everything down.


That’s why many Nigerians are now choosing digital alternatives instead of relying solely on domiciliary accounts.

Yes. Today, you can receive USD in Nigeria without opening a traditional domiciliary account.
